title: TrueNorth progress snapshot
description: The whole persisted state: what SaveCodec.encode writes, what a player pastes back in from an exported save, and what ProgressRepository stores in IndexedDB (localStorage is the fallback where IndexedDB is unavailable - ADR-0026). It is a document in every sense ADR-0007 means - authored by the previous session rather than by a content agent - and it is what SaveCodec.decode validates against before it trusts a byte of it. Storage is local only: no accounts, no server, no analytics (CLAUDE.md, Storage).

$schema.description: Present in the persisted document too, not only in authored content. An exported save that names its schema can be validated by the same tooling, and by a person, without guessing which build wrote it.

version.description: Save format version. SaveCodec migrates anything from minSupportedVersion up to its own version and refuses the rest cleanly.

character.description: The character the player made, or null before the creator has run. Nullable rather than absent because settings are persisted from the first screen, which is reachable before a character exists (TN-SAVE item 1).

lastPlayedLevelId.description: The level the player was last in, so the title screen can offer Continue. Null before any level has been entered. THE LEVEL, NOT THE SCREEN: TN-SAVE's survives table takes the level last played, and which screen the player was on is explicitly in the does-not-survive table. Restoring a player into a modal, a summary or a question card they have no context for is worse than putting them back on the map. Required rather than optional so that "no level yet" and "this build did not record one" are different states. Nothing fails closed without it - Choose a level still reaches every unlocked level - so it is a convenience the save carries, not a dependency (OQ-FLOW-4 / OQ-SAVE-7, ADR-0023).

exams.description: Finished attempts, oldest first. Every one of them has a finish time and a verdict; the exam the player has not finished yet is `examInProgress` and is not a row here (ADR-0027). An empty list is the normal state of a game where no exam has been taken and carries no floor - nothing folds it into a verdict (ADR-0024).

examInProgress.description: The one exam the player has started and not finished, or null. TN-ATTEMPT-04 asks that a document holding two unfinished attempts fail this schema; a nullable field holds at most one, so that document cannot be written down instead of being caught. Required rather than optional so "no exam in progress" and "this build did not record one" are different states, exactly as `lastPlayedLevelId` is.

playerCharacter.title: Player character document
playerCharacter.description: What the character creator produced: which character document the avatar uses, and the chosen option in every slot (TN-SAVE item 1, TN-CREATOR). There is no player-entered name - the creator asks for slot choices only, so nothing here is free text a player could be identified by.

skins.description: Slot name to chosen option id, one entry per selectable slot of that character document.

settings.title: Settings document
settings.description: Accessibility and comfort settings. Persisted, because a player should set them once (CLAUDE.md, Accessibility).

holdToChooseMs.description: TN-SET-09's single-switch hold time, in milliseconds. Persisted since save version 2: a switch user who set a two-second hold must not have to set it again next session, which is the least acceptable setting to lose.

volumeSettings.title: Volume settings
volumeSettings.description: One 0-1 level per audio bus. A fixed property set rather than a free map, because the buses are code, not content.

quests.description: One entry per quest the player has met, in any state. This replaces a completed-only list: TN-SAVE item 5 promises that "not offered / declined / accepted with the current step / completed" all come back, and a quest recorded only once it is finished cannot be resumed, which is the point of the story. Completion is `status: "completed"`; there is no second list saying the same thing.

stampEarnedAt.description: When this level's stamp was earned; null while it has not been. game.config's unlockRules.stampsToUnlockNext counts these, so a stamp is recorded, not derived from a rule that could change under a saved game.

questProgress.title: Quest progress document
questProgress.description: Where the player is in one quest. `offered` and `declined` are distinct from absent: a quest never met is not in this list at all, and TN-SAVE asserts that a declined quest comes back as declined rather than as never offered.

stepIndex.description: Index into the quest document's steps. 0 while offered or declined; the completed quest keeps the index of its last step.

stepProgress.description: How many of the current step's required items are done - questions answered on an `answer` step, 0 on every other kind. This is what lets "accepted, on step 2, two of three answered" survive a closed tab.

reviewState.title: Review state document
reviewState.description: FSRS card state for one question. The scheduler itself is pure domain (ADR-0001); this is only what it needs persisted.

firstReviewedAt.description: When this question was first answered; null while it has never been. `scheduler.dailyNewLimit` means "introduced today", and without this field the only marker of a new question is reps === 1, which stops being true the moment a question is answered twice - measured, that let 26 of 30 questions through a limit of 10 in one day. With it, exactly 10.

learningSteps.description: Which short-term step the question is on while its phase is learning or relearning; 0 otherwise. The next gap is read from this index, so a snapshot without it silently restarts the sequence after a reload - a question two steps into relearning comes back as if it had just lapsed.

phase.description: Where the question sits in the review cycle. Named `phase`, not `state`: "card state" is on TN-CARD-02's banned-vocabulary list, and a field the UI can read is a field the UI can leak. The four values are the model's, not the player's, and none of them is ever shown.

examAnswer.title: Exam answer document
examAnswer.description: One question of one attempt: what was asked, what the player chose, and what was right at the time. `subjectId` and `correctIndex` are copied down from the question bank on purpose - TN-RESULT-07 requires a result read a year later to keep its by-subject rows and its score when the question has left the build or its key has been corrected, and forbids recomputing a score from a bank that has changed. THERE IS NO `correct` FLAG: correctness is `chosenIndex === correctIndex`, so "unanswered, and correct" is a state that cannot be written down rather than one a conditional has to forbid (ADR-0027).

subjectId.description: The subject this question was drawn from, as the build that asked it knew. Recorded, not looked up: TN-RESULT-07 draws a by-subject row for a subject this build may no longer know.

chosenIndex.description: Which option the player chose, or null for UNANSWERED - a third state, distinct from wrong, that TN-EXAM-04 and TN-TIMER-05 both require the result to keep. Mutable until the exam ends: the card lets an answer be changed.

correctIndex.description: Which option was marked right when this question was asked. Four options, so 0-3 (question.schema.json fixes the tuple length).

examAttempt.title: Exam attempt document
examAttempt.description: One FINISHED run at the exam - a result. IRCC mirror: 20 questions, 15 to pass, 30 minutes, timer optional (CLAUDE.md, Purpose). An attempt that is still being taken is `examInProgress`, a different shape, so that `finishedAt` and `passed` are never asked to describe an exam nobody has finished (TN-ATTEMPT-01, ADR-0027). Every total is read out of `answers` and none is stored beside it: `askedQuestionIds` and `correctCount` were removed in save version 3 because a schema cannot check a stored total against the answers under it.

answers.description: Every question of the draw, in the order it was drawn, answered or not. `minItems: 1` because an exam with no questions is not an exam for any consumer, and an empty list reads as nothing wrong, nothing unanswered and no by-subject row to contradict the verdict beside it (ADR-0024). It is deliberately NOT pinned to game.config's exam.questionCount: a config change must not invalidate an attempt a player already made.

passed.description: Recorded, not derived. `exam.passMark` lives in game.config.json and may change under a saved result, the same reason `stampEarnedAt` is a recorded instant rather than a rule applied late.

timed.description: The timer is optional even in Exam mode; record whether it was on, so a result is never read as something it was not. A timer switched off mid-exam (TN-TIMER rule 4) records an untimed exam here.

examInProgress.title: Exam in progress document
examInProgress.description: The exam the player started and has not finished: the draw, the answers so far and the time left. It carries NO `finishedAt` and NO `passed`, because leaving an exam records neither (TN-ATTEMPT-01), and it is not a row in `exams`, because a nullable field holds at most one unfinished exam by construction (TN-ATTEMPT-04, ADR-0027).

answers.description: The twenty questions as drawn, with `chosenIndex` null for the ones not yet answered. This is what makes TN-ATTEMPT-02 true: the same questions in the same order, the answers given, and the skipped ones still skipped. Floored at 1 for the reason given on the finished attempt.

remainingMs.description: Milliseconds left on the clock, or null for AN UNTIMED EXAM. One field, not a number beside a boolean, so "timed with no time left recorded" cannot be written (ADR-0027). The clock always comes back paused (TN-ATTEMPT-02), so nothing records whether it was running. Milliseconds because every other duration in this codebase is; the clock still draws whole minutes (TN-TIMER rule 2).
